questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to survive in the wild with no food
Why spy films about bunkers are so popular
Why tech billionaires build luxury bunkers
How to store food safely for a long time
questions.why: They talk about luxury bunkers, the people building them and what they're afraid of.

questions.q: How prepared for disaster does Hannah say she is?
options: She has built her own bunker in the garden
She's organised, but has only a week's food
She has no food stored at home at all
She has enough food stored for a whole year
questions.why: Hannah says she's pretty organised but only has enough food to last about a week.

questions.q: What does Neil say about the billionaires' bunkers?
options: They are small and basic, with no windows
They are only used for storing food and water
They are open to the public at weekends
They are huge, with gyms and home cinemas
questions.why: He says they're huge, with cool features like gyms or home cinemas.

questions.q: Why has reporter Nathalie Jimenez thought about preparing for disaster?
options: She sees adverts for freeze-dried food on TV
She lived through a big earthquake as a child
A billionaire invited her to visit his bunker
She read a popular book about preppers
questions.why: She says US TV channels regularly show ads for freeze-dried food, about the prepper mentality.

questions.q: According to Nathalie, what are the billionaires afraid of?
options: Losing their companies to younger rivals
Being attacked at home by criminals
Nuclear war, AI risk and climate disaster
Rising house prices in big cities
questions.why: She lists nuclear tensions, AI risk and climate disaster, 'essentially any world-ending event'.

questions.q: What second reason does Nathalie give for building these bunkers?
options: They show the owner's high social status
They are a very good long-term investment
They are required by law in some states
They help protect the environment
questions.why: She says it's 'also a mark of societal status'.

questions.q: What would the bunkers allow billionaires to do in a disaster?
options: Help other people survive the disaster
Leave the planet in their own rockets
Keep working on their businesses as normal
Survive without giving up their luxury life
questions.why: Nathalie says they could live through it comfortably 'without compromising your lifestyle'.

questions.q: What does Nathalie suggest when she says the billionaires' fear is 'telling'?
options: That they are only pretending to be afraid
It's worrying, as they're building the future
That they will soon tell the public the dangers
That their bunkers are not really safe at all
questions.why: She says because they're building the future, the fact they're afraid of it is telling in itself.
